regime.skew: 25d call-rich (-0.28) while the 950 put wing cheapened 1.05 pt - no tail panic bid
regime.label: Dealer short gamma deepening 69% into a 13.3-point approach to the 960 put wall - max-pain failure now confirmed, the wall is an accelerant
evidence: -15,875 net GEX within 20 points of the 970 ATM, 69% deeper than yesterday's -9,411, and -18,216 across the whole 940-1150 ladder with no zero crossing anywhere: dealers sell into weakness at every strike, so today's -18.3 points was amplified rather than cushioned.

46.7 points now separate the 973.3 anchor from the 1020 max pain, up from 28.9 yesterday, while ATM IV expanded 1.40 pt to a 48-session high of 15.02% - price walking away from its anchor on expanding vol is the max-pain failure signature, which argues against fading back toward 1020.

1,419 contracts traded the 960 put on flat OI (-34 to 3,172), 3.2x its prior nine-session volume high of 438: the wall 13.3 points (1.44 sigma) below is live and being tested, but the turnover is two-way rather than fresh insurance.

1,342 OI at the 1010 call is the near-money wall and the first strike where per-strike net GEX turns positive (+525); it absorbed +216 OI on 648 lots today, pulling the structure's ceiling down from 1050 five sessions ago.

S50Z26.today_summary: 973.3 on the Dec future, -18.3 points (-1.85%) and the third-largest one-session drop of this series' 48 sessions, leaving price 13.3 points above the 960 put wall and 46.7 below the 1020 max-pain anchor. Put flow led at a 1.10 volume ratio against call-heavy 0.82 standing OI, and the 960 put alone traded 1,419 lots, 3.2x its prior nine-session high. Net GEX is negative at all 22 strikes (-18,216 total, -15,875 within 20 points of the 970 ATM), so dealer hedging accelerates rather than absorbs. ATM IV at 15.02% is a new 48-session high, which marks this as real flow rather than drift.
what_changed: The anchor fell 18.3 points to 973.3, widening the gap to the 1020 max pain from 28.9 to 46.7 points - 5.07x the 9.21-point 1-sigma daily move.
ATM net GEX deepened 69% to -15,875 from -9,411 as calls at 960-1010 absorbed +573 OI into the decline: the dealers' short-gamma burden grew fastest exactly where price now sits.
960-put volume jumped to 1,419 lots from 355, a 3.2x break of its nine-session range, yet OI slipped 34 to 3,172 - heavy two-way turnover at the wall, not new protection being built.
ATM IV rose 1.40 pt to 15.02%, taking out the 14.54% peak of 2026-11-21, while the 950 put wing cheapened 1.05 pt to 14.49% - the vol bid is concentrated near-money, not in the tail.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: The anchor has fallen 31.6 points from 1,004.9 on 2026-11-19 while max pain drifted only 10 points to 1020, so the spot-to-anchor gap widened from 25.1 to 46.7 points - price is walking away from the option structure, not toward it. Total net GEX has deepened monotonically for seven sessions, -1,179 on 2026-11-17 to -18,216 today, and has never once crossed zero, so there has been no long-gamma regime to reclaim at any point in the slide. Call OI added 2,484 contracts (+12.0%) and put OI 1,202 (+6.7%) across the five sessions, which rules out Unwind: the burden is accumulating. The near call wall migrated down 1050 to 1030 to 1010 while the 960 put wall held 3,213 to 3,172, compressing the structure's working range from 960-1050 to 960-1010. ATM IV expanded 13.12% to 15.02% over the same window - the confirmation that real flow is beating the option structure rather than returning to it.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 970 / 950
strategies.rationale: Short gamma at every strike plus a 13.3-point approach to the 960 wall is the matrix's break-below-the-put-wall cell: a break forces dealers to sell with the move, and the 961.3 breakeven sits exactly where that forced flow begins.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, approx 8.7 points at the 16.90 ask / 8.20 bid (approx 8.1 at mids). Max gain 20 - debit, approx 11.3 points below 950. Breakeven approx 961.3.
strategies.invalidation: A close back above 1010, the 1,342-OI near call wall and the first strike where per-strike net GEX turns positive (+525).

strategies.name: Put debit spread 950 / 940, armed only on a close below 960
strategies.rationale: The 950 put wing cheapened 1.05 pt to 14.49% IV today while the 1010 put richened 2.14 pt, so the continuation leg below the wall is the cheapest vol in the chain if a 960 break hands the move to dealer selling into the 879-contract 940 shelf.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, approx 2.7 points at the 9.00 ask / 6.30 bid. Max gain 10 - debit, approx 7.3 points below 940. Breakeven approx 947.3.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close holding above 960, the 3,172-contract put wall - without the break there is no forced dealer selling to carry price to 940.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1010 / 1030
strategies.rationale: Max pain 1020 sits 46.7 points (5.07 sigma) above spot with IV at a 48-session high, so selling the 1010 ceiling expresses the max-pain-failure read that price does not travel back to the anchor; short-vol payoff is negative-skew, so size it small.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20 - net credit, approx 17.6 points at the 4.70 bid / 2.30 ask. Max gain approx 2.4 points - the thinnest reward of the three, carried only by the 1010 wall.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1010 on expanding call volume, which flips per-strike net GEX positive and puts the 1020 max-pain anchor back in play.

S50Z26.prediction: 973.3 with dealers short gamma at all 22 strikes argues for downside follow-through rather than reversion, and the 9.21-point 1-sigma puts the 960 put wall within roughly 1.5 sessions. A close under 960 hands the move to dealer selling into the chain's deepest short-gamma shelf, where 879 contracts of 940 put OI mark the next node; the 1020 max pain, 46.7 points and 5.07 sigma away with 33 days left, is not a realistic magnet. A reclaim of 1010 invalidates the bearish read - that is where net GEX turns positive and the 1,342-contract call wall now sits.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no position sizing is implied. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind pinning and max-pain gravity are structurally weaker here than for share-settled single stocks: treat every wall and anchor as a tendency, not a guarantee. Defined-risk is not risk-free - the capped max loss on each structure above is real and can be realised in full. The 960 put wall turned over 1,419 lots on OI that fell 34, so part of that burden may be closing rather than fresh protection, and macro or news flow can override the option structure outright.
